Topic:Matildas

The Matildas returned to winning ways with a thumping win over Haiti. (Getty Images: Football Australia/Catherine Steenkeste)

Midfielder Leticia McKenna bagged a first-half brace to bolster her case for a first 2027 Women's World Cup call-up as the Matildas overcame Haiti 7–1.

Fresh off a humbling 4–2 defeat to powerhouses Germany, and without Arsenal star Steph Catley (managed), Australia got their World Cup preparations back on track in Chambly, France.

McKenna was the spark, as she produced two classy strikes before an own goal by Haiti defender Kethna Louis on the even of the break.

Then goals from Caitlin Foord, Daniela Galić, Clare Wheeler and Holly McNamara completed the victory.

Coach Joe Montemurro flagged in his pre-match press conference that he planned to switch things up as he looked to get a clearer picture of his side before next year's global showpiece event in Brazil.

Questions loomed over captain and star striker Sam Kerr's fitness after she complained of ankle soreness following the German clash, but she was also influential, playing a big role in two of the goals.

The rousing victory helped the Matildas firmly keep their number 15 world ranking, which currently puts them in pot two out of four for the World Cup draw, meaning a mathematically better chance for a more favourable draw.

It wasn't all smooth sailing for Montemurro's players, though, as their first-half defence looked timid when their Caribbean opponents employed their counterattack.

But they utterly dominated the second half as Haiti's wheels fell off, and gave Matildas fans plenty to cheer for, including a Kerr-Foord combination goal and Wheeler and McNamara each with their fourth international goals.

Catch up on all the action through the live blog below.

By Marnie Vinall

Key Event

By Marnie Vinall

That'll do us. Thank you for joining us this morning!

A wrap incase you missed it:

Leticia McKenna has made the most of her first chance in the Matildas starting side, scoring two goals in Australia's 7-1 win over Haiti in France.

Despite taking a 2-1 lead into half-time, thanks to McKenna's double, the Matildas were tested against world number 47 Haiti, 32 spots below Australia in the FIFA rankings.

But the Australians powered on in the second half to secure a dominant win, and end this international window on a high after falling to Germany four nights earlier.

By Marnie Vinall

One impressive thing from Matilda’s attack is that they are always looking to score given any possible opportunity not just playing the ball around in circles. The Socceroos could take note.

- Phillip

It was pleasing to see Australia handle the ball well in their top third and make the important touches to score.

By Marnie Vinall

Thank you for this morning's game updates, keeping us in the game. Great to know what’s happening when we don’t have access to tv coverage. Cheers. K

-  Kim J

We love to hear it, thanks Kim!

Key Event

By Marnie Vinall

Matildas finished with a succession of goals, taking a comprehensive 7-1 win over Haiti.

A great bounce back from the Germany defeat in this October window, with Australia enjoying five different goal scorers.

AUS 7 - 1 HAI, full-time

Key Event

By Marnie Vinall

Holly McNamara now adds her name to the scoresheet! That's her fourth international goal.

McNamara from distance sent the ball towards the net, Caitlin Foord was lurking nearby and watched closely to make sure the ball went through, while giving McNamara her moment.

AUS 7 - 1 HAI, 89 minutes

By Marnie Vinall

Australia are just having ping after ping at the goal now. Haiti are trying to get one back, but can't get a lot of possession.

Matildas with a lot of newer talent on the park to enjoy these last minutes.

AUS 6 - 1 HAI, 85 minutes

By Marnie Vinall

Cailtlin Foord almost had another goal for Australia, but just shot the ball wide and to the left of the net.

AUS 6 - 1 HAI, 84 minutes

By Marnie Vinall

On: Chloe Lincoln, Alex Chidiac, Jamilla Rankin, Tori Tumeth

Off: Mackenzie Arnold, Charli Grant, Clare Wheeler, Wini Heatley

AUS 6 - 1 HAI, 80 minutes

Key Event

By Marnie Vinall

The Matildas are having a bit of fun now. This time, Clare Wheeler.

Wheeler was looking to cross in but the ball floated straight into the net. That's her fourth international goal, and a deserved one after working so hard in this national side.

AUS 6 - 1 HAI, 79 minutes

Key Event

By Marnie Vinall

It's debut goal for Daniela Galic! She got on the end of a brilliant pass from Alana Murphy.

Galic took control just to the right outside the 18-yard box. She used her first touch to take possession and then had a great strike with her second. It sliced through to the back of the net.

And boy, she looked happy about it. Her first goal for her country.

AUS 5 - 1 HAI, 72 minutes

By Marnie Vinall

With 20 mintues to go, it's a good chance for the subs to get some important minutes into them. Australia are needing to get some more experience into the new guard before the Women's World Cup next year.

It comes at a good time in the match, with Australia holding a comfortable lead, while still needing to stay alert and aim to keep control.

AUS 4 - 1 HAI, 70 minutes

By Marnie Vinall

That's a host of changes to the Australian side.

On: Remy Siemsen, Alexia Apostolakis, Daniela Galic, Holly McNamara

Off: Kaitlyn Torpey, Sam Kerr, Hayley Raso, Leticia McKenna

Key Event

By Marnie Vinall

Now it's Cailtin Foord! And it's the Foord-Kerr combo we love to see.

Kerr passes the ball off to Foord, who was lurking just left of the net. She struck it beautifully, to send it straight into the back of the net.

That's a very comfortable lead Australia have now.

AUS 4 - 1 HAI, 64 minutes

By Marnie Vinall

Wini Heatley had a well-timed challenge on an Haiti player, who was streaming down the left wing. It was a great tackle to stop the run towards goal, and a moment to hopefully give Heatley some confidence.

AUS 3 - 1 HAI, 63 minutes

By Marnie Vinall

Australia have a comfortable lead now 3-1, but it's very important the Matildas don't get too complicant.

Haiti are still showing glimpses of some good attacking football, which could catch Australia out. Haiti have charged a few times towards Mackenzie Arnold's yet, as they move with such pace.

AUS 3 - 1 HAI, 61 minutes

Key Event

By Marnie Vinall

Sam Kerr forced the own goal.

By Marnie Vinall

I've just joined the blog at HT; maybe you have covered this earlier. What is our record against Haiti?

- Greg

Australia have only ever come up against Haiti once before, in 2012, where the Matildas won 4-0.

Key Event

By Marnie Vinall

Matildas got their third goal! It came from Sam Kerr, but will be an official own goal from Haiti, as it ball came off the defender's boot.

Kerr crossed it in, the Haiti defender tried to save it but could only make contact.

That should give the Matildas a good injection of confidence.

AUS 3 - 1 HAI, 52 minutes

By Marnie Vinall

Alana Murphy was oh so close to scoring the Matildas third goal, with the right foot touch sending the ball perfectly towards the net.

It was a fingertip save from the Haiti keeper.

AUS 2 - 1 HAI, 50 minutes
